newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt ends lower after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German debt ends lower after U.S. data.

text.p: German Bunds fell into negative territory in late post-bourse trade on Thursday afternoon as a fall in U.S. Treasuries dragged German debt lower in thin pre-Easter trade.

U.S. Treasuries were hit by stronger-than-expected jobs data. U.S. weekly jobless claims for the week ended March 22 were reported down 4,000 applicants at 310,000, after expectations of a drop of 2,000 claims.
The Bund future, which had traded in a relatively narrow band between 99.90 points and 100.47 points over the day, stood at 99.98 points, down 0.28 points, at the end of trade.

Next week's rash of German economic data, including February industrial production, expected on Tuesday, and February industrial orders, expected on Wednesday, would have were not the main area of interest for the German debt market, dealers said.
More important for interest rates was U.S. data, with market players closely examining the situation to see any clues to the next possible move on rates by the Federal Reserve.
The ten-year Bund stood at 100.47 points at the close, having traded as high as 100.99, with yields at 5.93 percent.
